primary_source.title: York-Antwerp Rules 2016
primary_source.held: not committed to this repository — see YAR_SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md
primary_source.note: Objects other than those listed in scope_verified have NOT yet been checked against this source. See YAR_SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md for defects observed but deliberately left uncorrected under TS-P03 scope.

definitions.text: In no case shall there be any allowance for sacrifice or expenditure unless reasonably made or incurred.
definitions.note: A reasonableness gate, not a fault gate. Per the Rule of Interpretation it overrides both the lettered and the numbered Rules; it says nothing about the fault of the party claiming.

definitions.text: There is a general average act when, and only when, any extraordinary sacrifice or expenditure is intentionally and reasonably made or incurred for the common safety for the purpose of preserving from peril the property involved in a common maritime adventure.

Only such losses, damages or expenses which are the direct consequence of the general average act shall be allowed as general average. Loss or damage sustained by the cargo or ship as a consequence of delay, whether on the voyage or subsequently, such as market loss, is not allowed as general average.

Rights to contribution in general average shall not be affected, though the event which gave rise to the sacrifice or expenditure may have been due to the fault of one of the parties to the common maritime adventure, but this shall not prejudice any remedies or defences which may be open against or to that party in respect of such fault.
definitions.note: Corrected 2026-08-15 (TSCR-6). The prior text read 'parties to the adventure' with a semicolon before 'but' — that is the YAR 1994 wording, carried under a YAR 2016 label. Rule D preserves the right to contribution notwithstanding fault and relocates the consequence of fault into remedies and defences under the applicable law; it does not bar the party at fault from claiming.

definitions.text: (a) Expenditure incurred by the parties to the common maritime adventure in the nature of salvage, whether under contract or otherwise, shall be allowed in general average provided that the salvage operations were carried out for the purpose of preserving from peril the property involved in the common maritime adventure and subject to the provisions of paragraphs (b), (c) and (d). … (d) Special compensation payable to a salvor by the shipowner under Article 14 of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989 to the extent specified in paragraph 4 of that Article or under any other provision similar in substance (such as SCOPIC) shall not be allowed in general average and shall not be considered a salvage expenditure as referred to in paragraph (a) of this Rule.
definitions.text_scope: Paragraphs (a) and (d) verbatim — these are the two limbs that carry the legal proposition. Paragraphs (b) and (c) are represented structurally in the fields below rather than reproduced, to keep source reproduction in this public repository to the minimum the object model requires. See YAR_SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md.
definitions.paragraph_b_gateways: Notwithstanding (a), where the parties to the common maritime adventure have separate contractual or legal liability to salvors, salvage shall only be allowed should any of five stated circumstances arise: (i) a subsequent accident or other circumstances resulting in loss or damage to property during the voyage that results in significant differences between salved and contributory values; (ii) significant general average sacrifices; (iii) salved values manifestly incorrect together with a significantly incorrect apportionment of salvage expenses; (iv) any party to the salvage has paid a significant proportion of salvage due from another party; (v) a significant proportion of the parties have satisfied the salvage claim on substantially different terms. For limb (v) no regard is had to interest, currency correction or the legal costs of either the salvor or the contributing interest.
definitions.paragraph_c: Salvage expenditures referred to in paragraph (a) include any salvage remuneration in which the skill and efforts of the salvors in preventing or minimising damage to the environment, such as is referred to in Article 13 paragraph 1(b) of the International Convention on Salvage, 1989, have been taken into account.
definitions.note: Corrected 2026-08-15 (TSCR-9). The prior text read 'Salvage payments, including interest and legal costs, shall not be allowed in general average' and treated Article 14 / SCOPIC special compensation as 'particular charges'. The first limb was the YAR 2004 Rule VI(a) position carried under a YAR 2016 label — an inversion of the legal proposition, not merely a source-fidelity defect. YAR 2016 Rule VI(a) ALLOWS salvage expenditure in general average where the operation was carried out to preserve the property from peril, subject to (b), (c) and (d). The exclusion in the 2016 edition is confined to VI(d): Article 14 special compensation and SCOPIC. The phrase 'particular charges' appears in neither edition and was not source text.
definitions.edition_history: YAR 1994 Rule VI(a) allowed salvage expenditure in general average. YAR 2004 Rule VI(a) removed it — salvage payments 'shall lie where they fall and shall not be allowed in general average', subject only to a credit/debit proviso where one party paid another's proportion. YAR 2016 Rule VI(a) restores a QUALIFIED allowance. Verified 2026-08-15 against CMI YAR 2016 (sha256 0c364edb…), CMI YAR 2004 (sha256 b9e6c79a…) and the CMI 1994/2004/2016 tabular comparison (sha256 c21b9482…).

definitions.text: The contributory value of the property shall be the value at the time and place when and where the adventure ends, determined in accordance with the contract of affreightment and the law applicable thereto. The value of cargo shall be the value at the time of discharge, ascertained from the commercial invoice rendered to the receiver or, if there is no such invoice, from the shipped value. The value of the ship shall be the value at the time of discharge, ascertained from the market value or, if there is no market value, from the insured value. The value of freight at risk shall be the amount at risk under the contract of affreightment.
